title: Mathematics in Industry Study Group (MISG) 2026
summary: Participated in the MISG 2026 at Wits University to solve real-world industrial problems through mathematical modeling.
content:
Selected as part of the AIMS South Africa Master's in Mathematical Sciences cohort by Dr. Jacques Rabie (Mathematics Innovation Manager), I had the opportunity to participate in the Mathematics in Industry Study Group (MISG) 2026, held at the University of the Witwatersrand (Wits) in Johannesburg, from January 19 to 23, 2026.

The MISG is a five-day collaborative workshop bringing together academic researchers and postgraduate students with industry representatives, around concrete research problems submitted by local companies. My participation was preceded by a preparatory Graduate Modelling Camp (January 14–17, 2026), held at the same venue, aimed at giving students additional practical experience in mathematical modeling applied to industrial problems.

The work done: during the study group, I contributed to solving industrial problems through mathematical modeling, notably on:
- corrosion inhibition, by modeling the chemical and physical mechanisms to slow down the degradation of metallic materials;
- deep-sea mining, by modeling the processes related to the extraction of underwater mineral resources.

At the end of the MISG, I wrote a report detailing the modeling work done, which was evaluated by the organizers, and then presented during a session dedicated to AIMS. This participation academically counted for two review courses as part of my Master's.

title: AIMS South Africa — Integrative Think Tank (ITT) 2026
summary: Participated in the Integrative Think Tank (ITT) 2026. Won 1st prize with the team on a sports analytics project in partnership with Laduma Analytics.
content:
🏆 1st Prize — R1 500

As part of my Master's in Mathematical Sciences at the African Institute for Mathematical Sciences (AIMS) South Africa, I participated in the Integrative Think Tank (ITT) 2026, a 5-day hackathon (April 13–17, 2026) organized by Dr. Jacques Rabie, Mathematics Innovation Manager at AIMS. The ITT brings together Master's students and industrial partners to solve concrete R&D problems in teams, with final presentations ("pitches") judged and rewarded with cash prizes.

The Team:
- Mannondé Gbaguidi
- Prince Anani
- Solomon Aniekan Charlie
- Vanessa Kouam Kenmogne
- Hassana Alhassan
- Lavender Akinyi Ayako

The Project: in partnership with Laduma Analytics, a South African company specializing in sports analytics, our team developed a predictive model for football match outcomes, applied to the South African Premier Soccer League (PSL). The model, trained on data from the 2024/25 season and tested under real conditions (out-of-sample) on the 2025/26 season, combined machine learning (Random Forest) and feature engineering to predict match results.

Result: our final presentation won the 1st prize (R1 500) of the hackathon. Following the event, we developed a complete web platform for the project (WebUnderscore) and shared it with Laduma Analytics, who were impressed by the work done and proposed a follow-up collaboration to explore the possibilities of developing and scaling the model.

title: AI Research Foundations for Higher Education Programme — Pilot Workshop 2026
summary: Participation in the Pilot Workshop of the AI Research Foundations for Higher Education program organized by AIMS South Africa and Google DeepMind.
content:
In 2026, I had the opportunity to participate in the Pilot Workshop of the AI Research Foundations for Higher Education program, organized in Muizenberg by AIMS South Africa (African Institute for Mathematical Sciences), in partnership with Google DeepMind, Google.org, the FATE Foundation, as well as UCL Computer Science and the UCL Centre for AI.

This "Train the Trainer" type program allowed me to deepen both the technical content of the AI Research Foundations course designed by Google DeepMind, and the pedagogical practices necessary to effectively transmit this knowledge in higher education. Beyond the technical content, the emphasis was placed on innovative teaching approaches, designed to make AI accessible to a diverse academic audience.

Beyond the working sessions, it was also an opportunity to meet other trainers and researchers from different backgrounds, in a studious and warm setting, conducive to discussion.

title: ICAMMDA Workshop on Machine Learning Modelling
summary: Participated in the ICAMMDA Workshop with Prof. Christopher Thron as guest speaker.
content: ICAMMDA Workshop on Machine Learning Modelling, held at the Federal University Oye-Ekiti (FUOYE) in Nigeria from August 3 to 21, 2026. The event featured Professor Christopher Thron (Texas A&M University-Central Texas) as the invited speaker. We explored the foundations of ML models, particularly tree-based models, as well as the formulation of research questions and the development of effective modeling strategies.
